message.reasoning:
We need to produce a JUnit 4 test file named FormElementTest.java, with all methods in FormElement tested comprehensively: constructor, elements(), addElement(), removeChild (via inheritance), submit(), formData() covering various cases.

We need to import Jsoup library classes; need to create Elements, Tag, Attributes, etc. Use Jsoup.parse to create Document with baseUri.

Test cases:

1. testAddElementAndElementsList: create FormElement with Tag.valueOf("form") maybe Tag.valueOf("form")? Tag.valueOf requires tag name; ensure baseUri. Add a child element (input) and verify elements() contains it.

2. testRemoveChildUpdatesElements: add element, then removeChild (via calling removeChild on FormElement). Since removeChild is protected, we can use reflection or subclass to expose it. Simpler: create a subclass in test that extends FormElement with public method exposeRemoveChild(Node). Or use reflection to invoke protected method.

3. testSubmitCreatesConnectionWithCorrectMethodAndUrl: Need to set action attribute and method attribute. Use FormElement with baseUri "http://example.com". Set action="/submit". Add no elements. Call submit() and verify connection's request URL and method. Jsoup.connect returns HttpConnection; we can inspect its request via connection.request(). But Jsoup's Connection interface doesn't expose request directly; however HttpConnection implements Connection and has request() method returning Connection.Request. In test, we can cast to HttpConnection and then get request. Or use reflection to get private fields. Simpler: we can use Jsoup.connect returns HttpConnection; we can cast.

Check that method GET for default, POST when method attr "post". Also test that when no action attribute, baseUri used.

Also test that IllegalArgumentException when action URL empty (no baseUri). But FormElement's submit uses baseUri() (from Element) which returns baseUri passed to constructor. If baseUri empty and no action attr, then Validate.notEmpty will throw. So we can create FormElement with empty baseUri and no action, expect exception.

4. testFormDataVariousControls: Build a form with many inputs:

- input type="text" name="username" value="john"
- input type="password" name="pass" value="secret"
- input type="checkbox" name="subscribe" checked and value "yes"
- input type="checkbox" name="unchecked" not checked
- input type="radio" name="gender" value="male" checked
- input type="radio" name="gender" value="female" not checked
- select name="city" with options: <option value="NY" selected>NY</option>, <option value="LA">LA</option>
- select name="country" with no selected option: options: <option value="US">US</option>, <option value="CA">CA</option> (first chosen)
- input without name should be ignored
- disabled input should be ignored.

Add these elements to form via addElement.

Then call formData() and verify list of KeyVals contains expected pairs, order as added.

Need to construct Elements manually: create Element objects with Tag.valueOf("input") etc. Set attributes via attr method.

Also for select, need to have child option elements. Use Element select = new Element(Tag.valueOf("select"), "", new Attributes()); etc; then add options.

Make sure tag().isFormSubmittable() works: For input, select, textarea; but we can trust.

Test that for checkbox without checked attribute not included, and for checked with empty value defaults to "on". Provide one without value.

Edge case: checkbox with empty value but checked.

Also test that disabled attribute excluded.

Also test that option selection fallback to first option if none selected.

5. testFormDataSelectNoOptions: ensure no exception and no data added.

6. Possibly test that formData returns copy (modifying returned list does not affect internal). Not needed but could.

Write JUnit 4 test class with @Test methods, using assertions from org.junit.Assert.

Will need to import org.jsoup.nodes.*; org.jsoup.helper.HttpConnection; org.jsoup.Connection.

Make sure to create Tag via Tag.valueOf("form") etc.

Potential issues: Tag.valueOf may require known tags; but we can use Tag.valueOf("form") which is allowed.

Attributes: new Attributes(); then put.

Define helper method createInput(String type, String name, String value, boolean checked, boolean disabled). Use Element input = new Element(Tag.valueOf("input"), "", new Attributes()); then set attrs.

Similarly for select.

Note that Element.val() returns attribute "value" for inputs and selected option for select? For select, val() returns value of first selected option? The code uses option.val() which returns attribute "value" of option element; if not present, option's own text? We'll set value attr.

Now write tests.

Also test that submit throws IllegalArgumentException when action cannot be determined.

Now produce final output with delimiters.
